content.text:
**Source for the four-die cancellation.** The only support is the incoming source record itself: the article sentence "The more powerful version of the upcoming Rubin Ultra chip with four compute dies has also been canceled." It is also carried as other_source_records item:e5, with original source SemiAnalysis (2026-07-06) and tier rumour, relayed by The Decoder. No stored piece says this. The closest stored pieces (e70, e71) cover a Rubin Ultra rack slip and a PCB midplane problem, not a cancellation of the four-die version. So my claim that the four-die version was canceled has no stored-piece citation. I should not have written it into the support reasoning as though it were covered by the piece IDs.

I also made a second error. In the v13 statement I wrote "(incoming record, consistent with e101)". e101 reports the NVL72x2 scrapping and the Kyber delay. It does not mention the four-die cancellation, so "consistent with e101" was an incorrect attribution.

**The governing instruction for support_ids.** The procedure required each argument to list "the piece ids it rests on with their source quality", with the opposing ids listed separately. Stored pieces are the only items with IDs in the argument, so support_ids should contain only stored piece IDs. Items from the incoming record that are not stored pieces (such as item:e5) should have been named in the limitations or new_information text, not in support_ids.

**Why I chose these support IDs.** For the delay to 2028, I used e64, e66, e98, e100 and e101, because each states the Kyber delay to 2028 and most name the PCB midplane cause. For the manufacturing and rack-slip detail, I used e70 and e71. These are SemiAnalysis claims relayed by Yahoo Finance, so they are rumour-tier and not independent of the main claim.

**Two citation choices I considered and rejected:**
- **e99** (DCD: Kyber was originally slated for 2027, with 144 Rubin Ultra GPUs). This is useful baseline context, and it is the only stored piece tying Kyber to Rubin Ultra. I did not cite it as support because it establishes the original schedule, not the delay. It is a candidate for support on the Rubin Ultra linkage.
- **e67 and e96** (CNBC and MarketScale on Vera Rubin shipments in fall or Q3–Q4 2026). I rejected these because they concern the Vera Rubin platform's shipments, not Kyber or Rubin Ultra, so the period and definition do not match.

**What the texts state versus my inference:**
- *Stated:* SemiAnalysis said Kyber NVL144 was delayed to 2028 because the PCB midplane is hard to manufacture (e66, e101). It said the NVL72x2 alternative was scrapped after customer pushback (e101 and the incoming record). The article states that the four-die Rubin Ultra version was canceled and that only the two-die version remains, with roughly half the compute (item:e5 and item:e6). Nvidia said its "roadmap is intact" (e65, e72, e102).
- *My inference:* that the scrapping of NVL72x2 and the four-die cancellation "removes a stopgap path" for Kyber; that Kyber's launch depends on the four-die version, which the article does not state; that the "2028" date means a launch could fall anywhere in that year, which is my reading of the text; and the resulting lean against launch by 2027-12-31 and the unresolved view for 2028-12-31.

The v11 and v13 arguments should be corrected to say that the four-die cancellation rests only on the incoming record (item:e5), that it is single-source SemiAnalysis, and that the link to Kyber is inference.
